Gotcha—let’s do a clean, reproducible evaluation that mirrors your training split and reports rich metrics.

Below is a drop-in script FrogSoundProject/src/eval_from_loader.py that:

Rebuilds the same train/val split using the same --seed and --train-split defaults as your training script (so it should match your last run if you didn’t change them).

Loads models/frog_cnn_best.pt and models/label_map.json.

Evaluates on the validation set only.

Prints overall accuracy, macro/micro F1, and a per-class table.

Saves a confusion matrix PNG and a CSV of predictions.

eval_from_loader.py
# FrogSoundProject/src/eval_from_loader.py
import os, json, argparse, random, numpy as np
from glob import glob

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
from torch.utils.data import Dataset, DataLoader

from sklearn.metrics import accuracy_score, f1_score, precision_recall_fscore_support, confusion_matrix, classification_report
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

PROC_DIR = os.path.join("FrogSoundProject", "data", "processed")
MODEL_DIR = os.path.join("FrogSoundProject", "models")
DEFAULT_MODEL = os.path.join(MODEL_DIR, "frog_cnn_best.pt")
DEFAULT_LABELMAP = os.path.join(MODEL_DIR, "label_map.json")
DEFAULT_WHITELIST = os.path.join("FrogSoundProject", "data", "species_whitelist.txt")

# ---------- Dataset (same framing as train) ----------
class MFCCDataset(Dataset):
    def __init__(self, items, target_frames=100, add_channel_dim=True):
        self.items = items
        self.T = target_frames
        self.add_channel = add_channel_dim

    def __len__(self):
        return len(self.items)

    def _pad_or_crop(self, a):
        # a: (13, frames)
        c, t = a.shape
        if t < self.T:
            pad = np.zeros((c, self.T - t), dtype=a.dtype)
            a = np.concatenate([a, pad], axis=1)
        elif t > self.T:
            a = a[:, :self.T]
        return a

    def __getitem__(self, idx):
        path, y = self.items[idx]
        a = np.load(path)
        if a.ndim == 3:  # segments might be (13, T, 1)
            a = a.squeeze(-1)
        a = a.astype(np.float32)
        a = self._pad_or_crop(a)
        if self.add_channel:
            a = a[None, ...]  # (1, 13, T)
        return torch.from_numpy(a), y

# ---------- Simple CNN (same as train script) ----------
class SmallCNN(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, n_classes, in_ch=1):
        super().__init__()
        self.net = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(in_ch, 16, 3, padding=1), nn.BatchNorm2d(16), nn.ReLU(), nn.MaxPool2d((1,2)),
            nn.Conv2d(16, 32, 3, padding=1), nn.BatchNorm2d(32), nn.ReLU(), nn.MaxPool2d((1,2)),
            nn.Conv2d(32, 64, 3, padding=1), nn.BatchNorm2d(64), nn.ReLU(), nn.AdaptiveMaxPool2d((13, 25)),
        )
        self.classifier = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Flatten(),
            nn.Linear(64*13*25, 256), nn.ReLU(), nn.Dropout(0.3),
            nn.Linear(256, n_classes)
        )

    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.net(x)
        return self.classifier(x)

# ---------- Utilities ----------
def list_classes(proc_dir, whitelist_path=None):
    classes = []
    for d in sorted(os.listdir(proc_dir)):
        p = os.path.join(proc_dir, d)
        if os.path.isdir(p):
            # exclude junky names like before
            bad = {"inct17", "misc", "am_edited", "pm_edited"}
            if d.lower() in bad: 
                continue
            if whitelist_path and os.path.exists(whitelist_path):
                with open(whitelist_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                    allowed = {line.strip() for line in f if line.strip()}
                if d not in allowed: 
                    continue
            classes.append(d)
    return classes

def build_items(proc_dir, classes):
    items = []
    for i, cls in enumerate(classes):
        for fp in glob(os.path.join(proc_dir, cls, "*.npy")):
            items.append((fp, i))
    return items

def split_items(items, train_split=0.78, seed=1337):
    random.Random(seed).shuffle(items)
    n_train = int(len(items)*train_split)
    return items[:n_train], items[n_train:]

def plot_confusion(cm, class_names, out_png):
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10,10))
    im = ax.imshow(cm, interpolation='nearest')
    ax.figure.colorbar(im, ax=ax)
    ax.set(xticks=np.arange(cm.shape[1]),
           yticks=np.arange(cm.shape[0]),
           xticklabels=class_names, yticklabels=class_names,
           ylabel='True label', xlabel='Predicted label',
           title='Confusion Matrix (Validation)')
    plt.setp(ax.get_xticklabels(), rotation=90, ha="center")
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig(out_png, dpi=200)
    plt.close(fig)

def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Evaluate frog model on validation split.")
    ap.add_argument("--processed", default=PROC_DIR)
    ap.add_argument("--model", default=DEFAULT_MODEL)
    ap.add_argument("--label-map", default=DEFAULT_LABELMAP)
    ap.add_argument("--whitelist", default=DEFAULT_WHITELIST)
    ap.add_argument("--train-split", type=float, default=0.78)
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=1337)
    ap.add_argument("--frames", type=int, default=100)
    ap.add_argument("--batch", type=int, default=64)
    args = ap.parse_args()

    # Load classes from label_map to lock ordering to training
    with open(args.label_map, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        label_map = json.load(f)  # {"class_name": index}
    # invert to ordered by index
    classes = [None]*len(label_map)
    for k, v in label_map.items():
        classes[v] = k

    # Build dataset items (only for those classes)
    all_items = []
    for i, cls in enumerate(classes):
        for fp in glob(os.path.join(args.processed, cls, "*.npy")):
            all_items.append((fp, i))

    # Recreate split with same seed
    train_items, val_items = split_items(all_items, train_split=args.train_split, seed=args.seed)
    print(f"Classes: {len(classes)} | Train: {len(train_items)} | Val: {len(val_items)}")

    val_ds = MFCCDataset(val_items, target_frames=args.frames, add_channel_dim=True)
    val_loader = DataLoader(val_ds, batch_size=args.batch, shuffle=False, num_workers=0, pin_memory=True)

    # Model
    device = torch.device("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")
    model = SmallCNN(n_classes=len(classes))
    ckpt = torch.load(args.model, map_location="cpu")
    # ckpt may be state_dict or full model state_dict
    state_dict = ckpt if isinstance(ckpt, dict) and "state_dict" not in ckpt else ckpt.get("state_dict", ckpt)
    model.load_state_dict(state_dict)
    model.to(device)
    model.eval()

    y_true, y_pred = [], []
    with torch.no_grad():
        for xb, yb in val_loader:
            xb = xb.to(device, non_blocking=True)
            logits = model(xb)
            pred = torch.argmax(logits, dim=1).cpu().numpy().tolist()
            y_pred.extend(pred)
            y_true.extend(yb.numpy().tolist())

    # Metrics
    acc = accuracy_score(y_true, y_pred)
    f1_micro = f1_score(y_true, y_pred, average="micro")
    f1_macro = f1_score(y_true, y_pred, average="macro")
    prec, rec, f1, support = precision_recall_fscore_support(y_true, y_pred, labels=list(range(len(classes))), zero_division=0)

    print(f"\nOverall:")
    print(f"  Accuracy: {acc:.3f}")
    print(f"  F1 (micro): {f1_micro:.3f}")
    print(f"  F1 (macro): {f1_macro:.3f}")

    print("\nPer-class: name | n | precision | recall | f1")
    order = np.argsort(-support)  # show most supported first
    for idx in order[:20]:
        print(f"  {classes[idx]:<28} | {int(support[idx]):4d} | {prec[idx]:6.2f} | {rec[idx]:6.2f} | {f1[idx]:6.2f}")

    # Confusion matrix
    cm = confusion_matrix(y_true, y_pred, labels=list(range(len(classes))))
    os.makedirs(MODEL_DIR, exist_ok=True)
    cm_png = os.path.join(MODEL_DIR, "confusion_matrix_val.png")
    plot_confusion(cm, classes, cm_png)
    print(f"\n📈 Confusion matrix saved to: {cm_png}")

    # Save CSV of predictions
    out_csv = os.path.join(MODEL_DIR, "val_predictions.csv")
    with open(out_csv, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write("true_label,true_name,pred_label,pred_name\n")
        for t, p in zip(y_true, y_pred):
            f.write(f"{t},{classes[t]},{p},{classes[p]}\n")
    print(f"📝 Predictions CSV: {out_csv}")

    # Full classification report (string) saved too
    report_txt = os.path.join(MODEL_DIR, "classification_report.txt")
    with open(report_txt, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(classification_report(y_true, y_pred, target_names=classes, zero_division=0))
    print(f"📄 Detailed report: {report_txt}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# FrogSoundProject/src/eval_from_loader.py
import os, sys, json, argparse, random, traceback
import numpy as np
from glob import glob

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
from torch.utils.data import Dataset, DataLoader

from sklearn.metrics import accuracy_score, f1_score, precision_recall_fscore_support, confusion_matrix, classification_report
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")  # headless safe
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

PROC_DIR = os.path.join("FrogSoundProject", "data", "processed")
MODEL_DIR = os.path.join("FrogSoundProject", "models")
DEFAULT_MODEL = os.path.join(MODEL_DIR, "frog_cnn_best.pt")
DEFAULT_LABELMAP = os.path.join(MODEL_DIR, "label_map.json")
DEFAULT_WHITELIST = os.path.join("FrogSoundProject", "data", "species_whitelist.txt")

def log(msg, verbose=True):
    if verbose:
        print(msg, flush=True)

# ---------- Dataset ----------
class MFCCDataset(Dataset):
    def __init__(self, items, target_frames=100, add_channel_dim=True):
        self.items = items
        self.T = target_frames
        self.add_channel = add_channel_dim

    def __len__(self):
        return len(self.items)

    def _pad_or_crop(self, a):
        c, t = a.shape
        if t < self.T:
            pad = np.zeros((c, self.T - t), dtype=a.dtype)
            a = np.concatenate([a, pad], axis=1)
        elif t > self.T:
            a = a[:, :self.T]
        return a

    def __getitem__(self, idx):
        path, y = self.items[idx]
        a = np.load(path, mmap_mode=None)
        if a.ndim == 3:  # (13, T, 1)
            a = a.squeeze(-1)
        a = a.astype(np.float32)
        a = self._pad_or_crop(a)
        if self.add_channel:
            a = a[None, ...]  # (1, 13, T)
        return torch.from_numpy(a), y

# ---------- Model (same as train) ----------
class SmallCNN(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, n_classes, in_ch=1):
        super().__init__()
        self.net = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(in_ch, 16, 3, padding=1), nn.BatchNorm2d(16), nn.ReLU(), nn.MaxPool2d((1,2)),
            nn.Conv2d(16, 32, 3, padding=1), nn.BatchNorm2d(32), nn.ReLU(), nn.MaxPool2d((1,2)),
            nn.Conv2d(32, 64, 3, padding=1), nn.BatchNorm2d(64), nn.ReLU(), nn.AdaptiveMaxPool2d((13, 25)),
        )
        self.classifier = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Flatten(),
            nn.Linear(64*13*25, 256), nn.ReLU(), nn.Dropout(0.3),
            nn.Linear(256, n_classes)
        )

    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.net(x)
        return self.classifier(x)

def split_items(items, train_split=0.78, seed=1337):
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    rng.shuffle(items)
    n_train = int(len(items)*train_split)
    return items[:n_train], items[n_train:]

def plot_confusion(cm, class_names, out_png):
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10,10))
    im = ax.imshow(cm, interpolation='nearest')
    ax.figure.colorbar(im, ax=ax)
    ax.set(xticks=np.arange(cm.shape[1]),
           yticks=np.arange(cm.shape[0]),
           xticklabels=class_names, yticklabels=class_names,
           ylabel='True label', xlabel='Predicted label',
           title='Confusion Matrix (Validation)')
    plt.setp(ax.get_xticklabels(), rotation=90, ha="center")
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig(out_png, dpi=200)
    plt.close(fig)

def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Evaluate frog model on validation split.")
    ap.add_argument("--processed", default=PROC_DIR)
    ap.add_argument("--model", default=DEFAULT_MODEL)
    ap.add_argument("--label-map", default=DEFAULT_LABELMAP)
    ap.add_argument("--train-split", type=float, default=0.78)
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=1337)
    ap.add_argument("--frames", type=int, default=100)
    ap.add_argument("--batch", type=int, default=64)
    ap.add_argument("--verbose", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    v = args.verbose
    log("🔎 Starting evaluation…", v)
    log(f"CWD: {os.getcwd()}", v)
    log(f"Processed dir: {args.processed}", v)
    log(f"Model path   : {args.model}", v)
    log(f"Label map    : {args.label_map}", v)

    # Existence checks
    if not os.path.exists(args.processed):
        print(f"❌ Processed dir missing: {args.processed}"); sys.exit(1)
    if not os.path.exists(args.model):
        print(f"❌ Model missing: {args.model}"); sys.exit(1)
    if not os.path.exists(args.label_map):
        print(f"❌ Label map missing: {args.label_map}"); sys.exit(1)

    # Load label map (preserve class order used in training)
    with open(args.label_map, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        label_map = json.load(f)
    classes = [None]*len(label_map)
    for k, idx in label_map.items():
        classes[idx] = k
    if any(c is None for c in classes):
        print("❌ Label map indices are not contiguous from 0..N-1."); sys.exit(1)
    log(f"Classes: {len(classes)}", v)

    # Build items for these classes
    all_items = []
    missing_any = False
    for i, cls in enumerate(classes):
        cls_dir = os.path.join(args.processed, cls)
        fps = sorted(glob(os.path.join(cls_dir, "*.npy")))
        if len(fps) == 0:
            log(f"⚠️  No .npy found for class '{cls}' in {cls_dir}", v)
            missing_any = True
        for fp in fps:
            all_items.append((fp, i))
    if len(all_items) == 0:
        print("❌ No .npy files found for any class. Aborting."); sys.exit(1)

    # Split to match training seed/split
    train_items, val_items = split_items(all_items, train_split=args.train_split, seed=args.seed)
    log(f"Items: train {len(train_items)} | val {len(val_items)}", v)

    # DataLoader
    val_ds = MFCCDataset(val_items, target_frames=args.frames, add_channel_dim=True)
    val_loader = DataLoader(val_ds, batch_size=args.batch, shuffle=False, num_workers=0, pin_memory=True)

    # Model
    device = torch.device("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")
    log(f"Device: {device}", v)
    model = SmallCNN(n_classes=len(classes))
    ckpt = torch.load(args.model, map_location="cpu")
    state_dict = ckpt if isinstance(ckpt, dict) and "state_dict" not in ckpt else ckpt.get("state_dict", ckpt)
    model.load_state_dict(state_dict)
    model.to(device)
    model.eval()
    log("Model loaded.", v)

    # Inference
    y_true, y_pred = [], []
    with torch.no_grad():
        for xb, yb in val_loader:
            xb = xb.to(device, non_blocking=True)
            logits = model(xb)
            pred = torch.argmax(logits, dim=1).cpu().numpy().tolist()
            y_pred.extend(pred)
            y_true.extend(yb.numpy().tolist())
    log("Inference done.", v)

    # Metrics
    acc = accuracy_score(y_true, y_pred)
    f1_micro = f1_score(y_true, y_pred, average="micro")
    f1_macro = f1_score(y_true, y_pred, average="macro")
    prec, rec, f1, support = precision_recall_fscore_support(
        y_true, y_pred, labels=list(range(len(classes))), zero_division=0
    )

    print(f"\nOverall:")
    print(f"  Accuracy: {acc:.3f}")
    print(f"  F1 (micro): {f1_micro:.3f}")
    print(f"  F1 (macro): {f1_macro:.3f}")

    print("\nPer-class: name | n | precision | recall | f1 (top 20 by support)")
    order = np.argsort(-support)
    for idx in order[:20]:
        print(f"  {classes[idx]:<28} | {int(support[idx]):4d} | {prec[idx]:6.2f} | {rec[idx]:6.2f} | {f1[idx]:6.2f}")

    # Outputs
    os.makedirs(MODEL_DIR, exist_ok=True)
    cm = confusion_matrix(y_true, y_pred, labels=list(range(len(classes))))
    cm_png = os.path.join(MODEL_DIR, "confusion_matrix_val.png")
    plot_confusion(cm, classes, cm_png)
    print(f"\n📈 Confusion matrix saved to: {cm_png}")

    # Save CSV of predictions
    out_csv = os.path.join(MODEL_DIR, "val_predictions.csv")
    with open(out_csv, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write("true_label,true_name,pred_label,pred_name\n")
        for t, p in zip(y_true, y_pred):
            f.write(f"{t},{classes[t]},{p},{classes[p]}\n")
    print(f"📝 Predictions CSV: {out_csv}")

    # Detailed report
    report_txt = os.path.join(MODEL_DIR, "classification_report.txt")
    with open(report_txt, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(classification_report(y_true, y_pred, target_names=classes, zero_division=0))
    print(f"📄 Detailed report: {report_txt}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        main()
    except Exception as e:
        print("❌ Unhandled exception:", e)
        traceback.print_exc()
        sys.exit(1)

import os, json, argparse, random, numpy as np
from glob import glob

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
from torch.utils.data import Dataset, DataLoader

from sklearn.metrics import accuracy_score, f1_score, precision_recall_fscore_support, confusion_matrix, classification_report
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

PROC_DIR = os.path.join("FrogSoundProject", "data", "processed")
MODEL_DIR = os.path.join("FrogSoundProject", "models")
DEFAULT_MODEL = os.path.join(MODEL_DIR, "frog_cnn_best.pt")
DEFAULT_LABELMAP = os.path.join(MODEL_DIR, "label_map.json")
DEFAULT_WHITELIST = os.path.join("FrogSoundProject", "data", "species_whitelist.txt")

# ---------- Dataset (same framing as train) ----------
class MFCCDataset(Dataset):
    def __init__(self, items, target_frames=100, add_channel_dim=True):
        self.items = items
        self.T = target_frames
        self.add_channel = add_channel_dim

    def __len__(self):
        return len(self.items)

    def _pad_or_crop(self, a):
        # a: (13, frames)
        c, t = a.shape
        if t < self.T:
            pad = np.zeros((c, self.T - t), dtype=a.dtype)
            a = np.concatenate([a, pad], axis=1)
        elif t > self.T:
            a = a[:, :self.T]
        return a

    def __getitem__(self, idx):
        path, y = self.items[idx]
        a = np.load(path)
        if a.ndim == 3:  # segments might be (13, T, 1)
            a = a.squeeze(-1)
        a = a.astype(np.float32)
        a = self._pad_or_crop(a)
        if self.add_channel:
            a = a[None, ...]  # (1, 13, T)
        return torch.from_numpy(a), y

# ---------- Simple CNN (same as train script) ----------
class SmallCNN(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, n_classes, in_ch=1):
        super().__init__()
        self.net = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(in_ch, 16, 3, padding=1), nn.BatchNorm2d(16), nn.ReLU(), nn.MaxPool2d((1,2)),
            nn.Conv2d(16, 32, 3, padding=1), nn.BatchNorm2d(32), nn.ReLU(), nn.MaxPool2d((1,2)),
            nn.Conv2d(32, 64, 3, padding=1), nn.BatchNorm2d(64), nn.ReLU(), nn.AdaptiveMaxPool2d((13, 25)),
        )
        self.classifier = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Flatten(),
            nn.Linear(64*13*25, 256), nn.ReLU(), nn.Dropout(0.3),
            nn.Linear(256, n_classes)
        )

    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.net(x)
        return self.classifier(x)

# ---------- Utilities ----------
def list_classes(proc_dir, whitelist_path=None):
    classes = []
    for d in sorted(os.listdir(proc_dir)):
        p = os.path.join(proc_dir, d)
        if os.path.isdir(p):
            # exclude junky names like before
            bad = {"inct17", "misc", "am_edited", "pm_edited"}
            if d.lower() in bad: 
                continue
            if whitelist_path and os.path.exists(whitelist_path):
                with open(whitelist_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                    allowed = {line.strip() for line in f if line.strip()}
                if d not in allowed: 
                    continue
            classes.append(d)
    return classes

def build_items(proc_dir, classes):
    items = []
    for i, cls in enumerate(classes):
        for fp in glob(os.path.join(proc_dir, cls, "*.npy")):
            items.append((fp, i))
    return items

    return items[:n_train], items[n_train:]

Great—your eval script looks solid and matches the training setup (frames=100, same CNN, same split logic, label-map ordering). Here’s exactly how to run it and avoid the usual gotchas:

1) Make sure scikit-learn is installed in the same Python you use to run eval
python -V
python -m pip install -U pip setuptools wheel
python -m pip install "scikit-learn>=1.3,<1.6"
(If you run with a specific interpreter, replace python with its full path.)

2) Run evaluation
python FrogSoundProject/src/eval_from_loader.py --frames 100 --batch 64
What it does:

Loads FrogSoundProject\models\frog_cnn_best.pt and label_map.json

Rebuilds the same train/val split (seed=1337, train_split=0.78) from your processed data

Evaluates on the val portion

Saves:

Confusion matrix → FrogSoundProject\models\confusion_matrix_val.png

Predictions CSV → FrogSoundProject\models\val_predictions.csv

Full classification report → FrogSoundProject\models\classification_report.txt

Common pitfalls (quick fixes)
ImportError: sklearn → install with the same python -m pip you use to run the script (see step 1).

Size mismatch when loading model → make sure you’re evaluating the model you just trained (correct frog_cnn_best.pt) and that label_map.json is from the same training run.

Empty val set → ensure FrogSoundProject\data\species_whitelist.txt (if used) wasn’t changed after training. This script ignores whitelist and uses the classes from label_map.json—so you’re fine unless you moved/deleted processed files.

(Optional) Tweaks
Evaluate with a different split (to sanity-check robustness):

python FrogSoundProject/src/eval_from_loader.py --train-split 0.7 --seed 2025
Larger batch for speed on CPU is fine (e.g., --batch 128), memory permitting.

Run that and you’ll get accuracy, macro/micro F1 in the console, plus the confusion matrix and detailed report saved under models/.

Thought for 20s
You're hitting that because your label_map.json isn’t a simple {class_name: index} dict—the values are dicts (or it’s a list). I’ve hardened the eval script to accept any of these shapes:

{"hyla_versicolor": 0, "pseudacris_maculata": 1, ...}

["hyla_versicolor", "pseudacris_maculata", ...]

[{ "name": "hyla_versicolor", "index": 0}, ...] (or "idx")

[{"hyla_versicolor": 0}, {"pseudacris_maculata": 1}, ...]

{ "mapping": { "hyla_versicolor": 0, ... } }

Drop this in as FrogSoundProject/src/eval_from_loader.py:

# FrogSoundProject/src/eval_from_loader.py
import os, json, argparse, random, numpy as np
from glob import glob

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
from torch.utils.data import Dataset, DataLoader

from sklearn.metrics import accuracy_score, f1_score, precision_recall_fscore_support, confusion_matrix, classification_report
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

PROC_DIR = os.path.join("FrogSoundProject", "data", "processed")
MODEL_DIR = os.path.join("FrogSoundProject", "models")
DEFAULT_MODEL = os.path.join(MODEL_DIR, "frog_cnn_best.pt")
DEFAULT_LABELMAP = os.path.join(MODEL_DIR, "label_map.json")
DEFAULT_WHITELIST = os.path.join("FrogSoundProject", "data", "species_whitelist.txt")

# ---------- Dataset (same framing as train) ----------
class MFCCDataset(Dataset):
    def __init__(self, items, target_frames=100, add_channel_dim=True):
        self.items = items
        self.T = target_frames
        self.add_channel = add_channel_dim

    def __len__(self):
        return len(self.items)

    def _pad_or_crop(self, a):
        c, t = a.shape
        if t < self.T:
            pad = np.zeros((c, self.T - t), dtype=a.dtype)
            a = np.concatenate([a, pad], axis=1)
        elif t > self.T:
            a = a[:, :self.T]
        return a

    def __getitem__(self, idx):
        path, y = self.items[idx]
        a = np.load(path)
        if a.ndim == 3:
            a = a.squeeze(-1)
        a = a.astype(np.float32)
        a = self._pad_or_crop(a)
        if self.add_channel:
            a = a[None, ...]  # (1, 13, T)
        return torch.from_numpy(a), y

# ---------- Simple CNN (same as train script) ----------
class SmallCNN(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, n_classes, in_ch=1):
        super().__init__()
        self.net = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(in_ch, 16, 3, padding=1), nn.BatchNorm2d(16), nn.ReLU(), nn.MaxPool2d((1,2)),
            nn.Conv2d(16, 32, 3, padding=1), nn.BatchNorm2d(32), nn.ReLU(), nn.MaxPool2d((1,2)),
            nn.Conv2d(32, 64, 3, padding=1), nn.BatchNorm2d(64), nn.ReLU(), nn.AdaptiveMaxPool2d((13, 25)),
        )
        self.classifier = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Flatten(),
            nn.Linear(64*13*25, 256), nn.ReLU(), nn.Dropout(0.3),
            nn.Linear(256, n_classes)
        )

    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.net(x)
        return self.classifier(x)

# ---------- Label map normalization ----------
def normalize_label_map(obj):
    """
    Returns: classes list in index order: classes[idx] = name
    Accepts multiple shapes of label_map.json.
    """
    # Case A: dict of name -> index
    if isinstance(obj, dict):
        # Sub-case: wrapped mapping
        if "mapping" in obj and isinstance(obj["mapping"], dict):
            obj = obj["mapping"]
        # If keys are names and values are ints
        if all(isinstance(k, str) for k in obj.keys()) and all(isinstance(v, int) for v in obj.values()):
            max_idx = max(obj.values())
            classes = [None] * (max_idx + 1)
            for name, idx in obj.items():
                classes[int(idx)] = name
            return classes
        # Sub-case: dict of idx (as str/int) -> name
        if all(str(k).isdigit() for k in obj.keys()) and all(isinstance(v, str) for v in obj.values()):
            items = sorted(((int(k), v) for k, v in obj.items()), key=lambda x: x[0])
            return [name for _, name in items]
        # Sub-case: dict of name -> dict(...index/idx...)
        if all(isinstance(v, dict) for v in obj.values()):
            tmp = {}
            for name, inner in obj.items():
                if "index" in inner:
                    tmp[name] = int(inner["index"])
                elif "idx" in inner:
                    tmp[name] = int(inner["idx"])
                else:
                    raise ValueError("Unrecognized inner mapping format in label_map.json")
            max_idx = max(tmp.values())
            classes = [None] * (max_idx + 1)
            for name, idx in tmp.items():
                classes[idx] = name
            return classes
        raise ValueError("Unrecognized dict format for label_map.json")

    # Case B: list [...]
    if isinstance(obj, list):
        # list of names
        if all(isinstance(x, str) for x in obj):
            return list(obj)
        # list of single-pair dicts: [{"name": idx}] or [{"hyla": 0}, ...]
        if all(isinstance(x, dict) for x in obj):
            # try {"name": ..., "index"/"idx": ...}
            if all(("name" in x and ("index" in x or "idx" in x)) for x in obj):
                pairs = [(int(x.get("index", x.get("idx"))), x["name"]) for x in obj]
                pairs.sort()
                return [name for _, name in pairs]
            # try [{"hyla": 0}, {"pseudacris": 1}, ...]
            if all(len(x) == 1 for x in obj):
                tmp = {}
                for d in obj:
                    (name, idx), = d.items()
                    tmp[name] = int(idx)
                max_idx = max(tmp.values())
                classes = [None] * (max_idx + 1)
                for name, idx in tmp.items():
                    classes[idx] = name
                return classes
        raise ValueError("Unrecognized list format for label_map.json")

    raise ValueError("Unsupported label_map.json structure")

# ---------- Utilities ----------
def split_items(items, train_split=0.78, seed=1337):
    random.Random(seed).shuffle(items)
    n_train = int(len(items)*train_split)
    return items[:n_train], items[n_train:]

def plot_confusion(cm, class_names, out_png):
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10,10))
    im = ax.imshow(cm, interpolation='nearest')
    ax.figure.colorbar(im, ax=ax)
    ax.set(xticks=np.arange(cm.shape[1]),
           yticks=np.arange(cm.shape[0]),
           xticklabels=class_names, yticklabels=class_names,
           ylabel='True label', xlabel='Predicted label',
           title='Confusion Matrix (Validation)')
    plt.setp(ax.get_xticklabels(), rotation=90, ha="center")
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig(out_png, dpi=200)
    plt.close(fig)

def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Evaluate frog model on validation split.")
    ap.add_argument("--processed", default=PROC_DIR)
    ap.add_argument("--model", default=DEFAULT_MODEL)
    ap.add_argument("--label-map", default=DEFAULT_LABELMAP)
    ap.add_argument("--train-split", type=float, default=0.78)
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=1337)
    ap.add_argument("--frames", type=int, default=100)
    ap.add_argument("--batch", type=int, default=64)
    args = ap.parse_args()

    # Load classes from label_map (robust to various formats)
    with open(args.label_map, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        raw_map = json.load(f)
    classes = normalize_label_map(raw_map)

    # Build dataset items for those classes, in index order
    all_items = []
    for i, cls in enumerate(classes):
        cls_dir = os.path.join(args.processed, cls)
        for fp in glob(os.path.join(cls_dir, "*.npy")):
            all_items.append((fp, i))

    # Recreate split with same seed
    train_items, val_items = split_items(all_items, train_split=args.train_split, seed=args.seed)
    print(f"Classes: {len(classes)} | Train: {len(train_items)} | Val: {len(val_items)}")

    val_ds = MFCCDataset(val_items, target_frames=args.frames, add_channel_dim=True)
    val_loader = DataLoader(val_ds, batch_size=args.batch, shuffle=False, num_workers=0, pin_memory=True)

    # Model
    device = torch.device("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")
    model = SmallCNN(n_classes=len(classes))
    ckpt = torch.load(args.model, map_location="cpu")
    # Accept either a plain state_dict or {'state_dict': ...}
    state_dict = ckpt.get("state_dict", ckpt) if isinstance(ckpt, dict) else ckpt
    model.load_state_dict(state_dict)
    model.to(device)
    model.eval()

    y_true, y_pred = [], []
    with torch.no_grad():
        for xb, yb in val_loader:
            xb = xb.to(device, non_blocking=True)
            logits = model(xb)
            pred = torch.argmax(logits, dim=1).cpu().numpy().tolist()
            y_pred.extend(pred)
            y_true.extend(yb.numpy().tolist())

    # Metrics
    acc = accuracy_score(y_true, y_pred)
    f1_micro = f1_score(y_true, y_pred, average="micro", zero_division=0)
    f1_macro = f1_score(y_true, y_pred, average="macro", zero_division=0)
    prec, rec, f1, support = precision_recall_fscore_support(
        y_true, y_pred, labels=list(range(len(classes))), zero_division=0
    )

    print(f"\nOverall:")
    print(f"  Accuracy: {acc:.3f}")
    print(f"  F1 (micro): {f1_micro:.3f}")
    print(f"  F1 (macro): {f1_macro:.3f}")

    print("\nPer-class: name | n | precision | recall | f1")
    order = np.argsort(-support)
    for idx in order[:20]:
        print(f"  {classes[idx]:<28} | {int(support[idx]):4d} | {prec[idx]:6.2f} | {rec[idx]:6.2f} | {f1[idx]:6.2f}")

    cm = confusion_matrix(y_true, y_pred, labels=list(range(len(classes))))
    os.makedirs(MODEL_DIR, exist_ok=True)
    cm_png = os.path.join(MODEL_DIR, "confusion_matrix_val.png")
    plot_confusion(cm, classes, cm_png)
    print(f"\n📈 Confusion matrix saved to: {cm_png}")

    out_csv = os.path.join(MODEL_DIR, "val_predictions.csv")
    with open(out_csv, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write("true_label,true_name,pred_label,pred_name\n")
        for t, p in zip(y_true, y_pred):
            f.write(f"{t},{classes[t]},{p},{classes[p]}\n")
    print(f"📝 Predictions CSV: {out_csv}")

    report_txt = os.path.join(MODEL_DIR, "classification_report.txt")
    with open(report_txt, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(classification_report(y_true, y_pred, target_names=classes, zero_division=0))
    print(f"📄 Detailed report: {report_txt}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# ---------- Utilities ----------
def list_classes(proc_dir, whitelist_path=None):
    classes = []
    for d in sorted(os.listdir(proc_dir)):
        p = os.path.join(proc_dir, d)
        if os.path.isdir(p):
            # exclude junky names like before
            bad = {"inct17", "misc", "am_edited", "pm_edited"}
            if d.lower() in bad: 
                continue
            if whitelist_path and os.path.exists(whitelist_path):
                with open(whitelist_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                    allowed = {line.strip() for line in f if line.strip()}
                if d not in allowed: 
                    continue
            classes.append(d)
    return classes

def build_items(proc_dir, classes):
    items = []
    for i, cls in enumerate(classes):
        for fp in glob(os.path.join(proc_dir, cls, "*.npy")):
            items.append((fp, i))
    return items

def split_items(items, train_split=0.78, seed=1337):

    n_train = int(len(items)*train_split)
    return items[:n_train], items[n_train:]

    ap.add_argument("--batch", type=int, default=64)

Yup—the eval script you’re running assumes label_map.json is a plain {name: index} dict. Yours isn’t (one or more values are dicts/lists), so classes[v] = k blew up.

Here’s a drop-in replacement that robustly normalizes label_map.json (handles dict, list of names, list of objects, or {index:name}), reloads the exact class order used at train time, and evaluates + saves confusion matrix, CSV, and report.

Replace your file with this:

# FrogSoundProject/src/eval_from_loader.py
import os, json, argparse, random, numpy as np
from glob import glob

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
from torch.utils.data import Dataset, DataLoader

from sklearn.metrics import accuracy_score, f1_score, precision_recall_fscore_support, confusion_matrix, classification_report
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

PROC_DIR = os.path.join("FrogSoundProject", "data", "processed")
MODEL_DIR = os.path.join("FrogSoundProject", "models")
DEFAULT_MODEL = os.path.join(MODEL_DIR, "frog_cnn_best.pt")
DEFAULT_LABELMAP = os.path.join(MODEL_DIR, "label_map.json")
DEFAULT_WHITELIST = os.path.join("FrogSoundProject", "data", "species_whitelist.txt")

# ---------- Dataset ----------
class MFCCDataset(Dataset):
    def __init__(self, items, target_frames=100, add_channel_dim=True):
        self.items = items
        self.T = target_frames
        self.add_channel = add_channel_dim

    def __len__(self):
        return len(self.items)

    def _pad_or_crop(self, a):
        c, t = a.shape
        if t < self.T:
            pad = np.zeros((c, self.T - t), dtype=a.dtype)
            a = np.concatenate([a, pad], axis=1)
        elif t > self.T:
            a = a[:, :self.T]
        return a

    def __getitem__(self, idx):
        path, y = self.items[idx]
        a = np.load(path)
        if a.ndim == 3:
            a = a.squeeze(-1)
        a = a.astype(np.float32)
        a = self._pad_or_crop(a)
        if self.add_channel:
            a = a[None, ...]  # (1, 13, T)
        return torch.from_numpy(a), y

# ---------- Model (same as train) ----------
class SmallCNN(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, n_classes, in_ch=1):
        super().__init__()
        self.net = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(in_ch, 16, 3, padding=1), nn.BatchNorm2d(16), nn.ReLU(), nn.MaxPool2d((1,2)),
            nn.Conv2d(16, 32, 3, padding=1), nn.BatchNorm2d(32), nn.ReLU(), nn.MaxPool2d((1,2)),
            nn.Conv2d(32, 64, 3, padding=1), nn.BatchNorm2d(64), nn.ReLU(), nn.AdaptiveMaxPool2d((13, 25)),
        )
        self.classifier = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Flatten(),
            nn.Linear(64*13*25, 256), nn.ReLU(), nn.Dropout(0.3),
            nn.Linear(256, n_classes)
        )

    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.net(x)
        return self.classifier(x)

# ---------- Helpers ----------
def normalize_label_map(obj):
    """
    Accepts any of:
      - {"name": index, ...}
      - [{"name": "...", "index": i}, ...]
      - [{"name": "..."}, ...]  (indices = enumerate order)
      - ["name1","name2",...]   (indices = enumerate order)
      - {index: "name", ...}    (reverse mapping)
    Returns: ordered list of class names where position == index.
    """
    if isinstance(obj, dict):
        # detect dict direction
        # if keys are names -> values indices
        try:
            # values all ints?
            if all(isinstance(v, int) for v in obj.values()):
                n = max(obj.values()) + 1
                classes = [None] * n
                for name, idx in obj.items():
                    classes[idx] = name
                return classes
        except Exception:
            pass
        # maybe {index: name}
        try:
            if all(str(k).isdigit() for k in obj.keys()):
                items = {int(k): v for k, v in obj.items()}
                n = max(items.keys()) + 1
                classes = [None] * n
                for idx, name in items.items():
                    classes[idx] = name
                return classes
        except Exception:
            pass
        # fallback: treat keys as names in arbitrary order
        return list(obj.keys())

    if isinstance(obj, list):
        if not obj:
            return []
        # list of strings?
        if all(isinstance(x, str) for x in obj):
            return list(obj)
        # list of dicts with name/index?
        names = [None] * len(obj)
        has_index = all(isinstance(x, dict) and ("index" in x) for x in obj)
        if has_index:
            n = max(int(x["index"]) for x in obj) + 1
            names = [None] * n
            for x in obj:
                names[int(x["index"])] = x.get("name", str(x.get("label", "?")))
            return names
        # list of dicts without index: preserve order
        return [x.get("name", str(x.get("label", f"class_{i}"))) if isinstance(x, dict) else str(x)
                for i, x in enumerate(obj)]

    # unknown -> empty
    return []

def build_items(proc_dir, classes):
    items = []
    for i, cls in enumerate(classes):
        for fp in glob(os.path.join(proc_dir, cls, "*.npy")):
            items.append((fp, i))
    return items

def split_items(items, train_split=0.78, seed=1337):
    random.Random(seed).shuffle(items)
    n_train = int(len(items) * train_split)
    return items[:n_train], items[n_train:]

def plot_confusion(cm, class_names, out_png):
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10,10))
    im = ax.imshow(cm, interpolation='nearest')
    ax.figure.colorbar(im, ax=ax)
    ax.set(xticks=np.arange(cm.shape[1]),
           yticks=np.arange(cm.shape[0]),
           xticklabels=class_names, yticklabels=class_names,
           ylabel='True label', xlabel='Predicted label',
           title='Confusion Matrix (Validation)')
    plt.setp(ax.get_xticklabels(), rotation=90, ha="center")
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig(out_png, dpi=200)
    plt.close(fig)

def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Evaluate frog model on validation split.")
    ap.add_argument("--processed", default=PROC_DIR)
    ap.add_argument("--model", default=DEFAULT_MODEL)
    ap.add_argument("--label-map", default=DEFAULT_LABELMAP)
    ap.add_argument("--train-split", type=float, default=0.78)
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=1337)
    ap.add_argument("--frames", type=int, default=100)
    ap.add_argument("--batch", type=int, default=64)
    args = ap.parse_args()

    # Load & normalize label map to ordered class list
    with open(args.label_map, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        raw_map = json.load(f)
    classes = normalize_label_map(raw_map)
    if any(c is None for c in classes):
        # defensive clean if gaps exist
        classes = [c for c in classes if c is not None]
    print(f"Loaded {len(classes)} classes from label_map.json")

    # Build items only for those classes (keeps class order)
    all_items = build_items(args.processed, classes)

    # Recreate the same split
    train_items, val_items = split_items(all_items, train_split=args.train_split, seed=args.seed)
    print(f"Classes: {len(classes)} | Train: {len(train_items)} | Val: {len(val_items)}")

    val_ds = MFCCDataset(val_items, target_frames=args.frames, add_channel_dim=True)
    val_loader = DataLoader(val_ds, batch_size=args.batch, shuffle=False, num_workers=0, pin_memory=False)

    # Model
    device = torch.device("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")
    model = SmallCNN(n_classes=len(classes))
    ckpt = torch.load(args.model, map_location="cpu")

    # Accept either a raw state_dict or a wrapper dict
    if isinstance(ckpt, dict) and any(k.startswith("net.") or k.startswith("classifier.") for k in ckpt.keys()):
        state_dict = ckpt
    elif isinstance(ckpt, dict) and "state_dict" in ckpt:
        state_dict = ckpt["state_dict"]
    else:
        state_dict = ckpt

    model.load_state_dict(state_dict, strict=True)
    model.to(device)
    model.eval()

    # Eval
    y_true, y_pred = [], []
    with torch.no_grad():
        for xb, yb in val_loader:
            xb = xb.to(device, non_blocking=True)
            logits = model(xb)
            pred = torch.argmax(logits, dim=1).cpu().numpy().tolist()
            y_pred.extend(pred)
            y_true.extend(yb.numpy().tolist())

    # Metrics
    acc = accuracy_score(y_true, y_pred)
    f1_micro = f1_score(y_true, y_pred, average="micro")
    f1_macro = f1_score(y_true, y_pred, average="macro")
    prec, rec, f1, support = precision_recall_fscore_support(
        y_true, y_pred, labels=list(range(len(classes))), zero_division=0
    )

    print(f"\nOverall:")
    print(f"  Accuracy: {acc:.3f}")
    print(f"  F1 (micro): {f1_micro:.3f}")
    print(f"  F1 (macro): {f1_macro:.3f}")

    print("\nPer-class: name | n | precision | recall | f1")
    order = np.argsort(-support)
    for idx in order[:20]:
        print(f"  {classes[idx]:<28} | {int(support[idx]):4d} | {prec[idx]:6.2f} | {rec[idx]:6.2f} | {f1[idx]:6.2f}")

    # Confusion matrix
    cm = confusion_matrix(y_true, y_pred, labels=list(range(len(classes))))
    os.makedirs(MODEL_DIR, exist_ok=True)
    cm_png = os.path.join(MODEL_DIR, "confusion_matrix_val.png")
    plot_confusion(cm, classes, cm_png)
    print(f"\n📈 Confusion matrix saved to: {cm_png}")

    # Save CSV of predictions
    out_csv = os.path.join(MODEL_DIR, "val_predictions.csv")
    with open(out_csv, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write("true_label,true_name,pred_label,pred_name\n")
        for t, p in zip(y_true, y_pred):
            f.write(f"{t},{classes[t]},{p},{classes[p]}\n")
    print(f"📝 Predictions CSV: {out_csv}")

    # Full classification report
    report_txt = os.path.join(MODEL_DIR, "classification_report.txt")
    with open(report_txt, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(classification_report(y_true, y_pred, target_names=classes, zero_division=0))
    print(f"📄 Detailed report: {report_txt}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Thought for 11s
Great catch — your checkpoint isn’t a raw state_dict. It’s a wrapper dict with keys like model_state, classes, and frames, and your label_map.json currently resolves to only 1 class, so eval was (a) loading the wrong mapping and (b) trying to feed the wrong state into the model.

Here’s a drop-in eval script that:

Reads classes from the checkpoint if available (preferred), falling back to label_map.json.

Pulls the correct state_dict from ckpt["model_state"] (or other formats).

Uses ckpt["frames"] to set the input length unless you override --frames.

Gracefully exits if the validation set is empty (instead of crashing).

Replace your file with this:

from glob import glob

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
from torch.utils.data import Dataset, DataLoader

from sklearn.metrics import accuracy_score, f1_score, precision_recall_fscore_support, confusion_matrix, classification_report
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

PROC_DIR = os.path.join("FrogSoundProject", "data", "processed")
MODEL_DIR = os.path.join("FrogSoundProject", "models")
DEFAULT_MODEL = os.path.join(MODEL_DIR, "frog_cnn_best.pt")
DEFAULT_LABELMAP = os.path.join(MODEL_DIR, "label_map.json")

# ---------- Dataset ----------
class MFCCDataset(Dataset):
    def __init__(self, items, target_frames=100, add_channel_dim=True):
        self.items = items
        self.T = target_frames
        self.add_channel = add_channel_dim

    def __len__(self):
        return len(self.items)

    def _pad_or_crop(self, a):
        c, t = a.shape
        if t < self.T:
            pad = np.zeros((c, self.T - t), dtype=a.dtype)
            a = np.concatenate([a, pad], axis=1)
        elif t > self.T:
            a = a[:, :self.T]
        return a

    def __getitem__(self, idx):

        a = np.load(path)
        if a.ndim == 3:
            a = a.squeeze(-1)
        a = a.astype(np.float32)
        a = self._pad_or_crop(a)
        if self.add_channel:
            a = a[None, ...]  # (1, 13, T)
        return torch.from_numpy(a), y

class SmallCNN(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, n_classes, in_ch=1):
        super().__init__()
        self.net = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(in_ch, 16, 3, padding=1), nn.BatchNorm2d(16), nn.ReLU(), nn.MaxPool2d((1,2)),
            nn.Conv2d(16, 32, 3, padding=1), nn.BatchNorm2d(32), nn.ReLU(), nn.MaxPool2d((1,2)),
            nn.Conv2d(32, 64, 3, padding=1), nn.BatchNorm2d(64), nn.ReLU(), nn.AdaptiveMaxPool2d((13, 25)),
        )
        self.classifier = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Flatten(),
            nn.Linear(64*13*25, 256), nn.ReLU(), nn.Dropout(0.3),
            nn.Linear(256, n_classes)
        )

    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.net(x)
        return self.classifier(x)

# ---------- Helpers ----------
def normalize_label_map(obj):
    # Accept many shapes and return ordered list where idx == class id
    if isinstance(obj, dict):
        # name->idx
        if all(isinstance(v, int) for v in obj.values()):
            n = max(obj.values()) + 1
            classes = [None]*n
            for name, idx in obj.items():
                classes[idx] = name
            return classes
        # idx->name (even if keys are strings)
        if all(str(k).isdigit() for k in obj.keys()):
            items = {int(k): v for k, v in obj.items()}
            n = max(items.keys()) + 1
            classes = [None]*n
            for idx, name in items.items():
                classes[idx] = name
            return classes
        # fallback: dict keys as names
        return list(obj.keys())

    if isinstance(obj, list):
        if not obj:
            return []
        if all(isinstance(x, str) for x in obj):
            return list(obj)
        if all(isinstance(x, dict) and ("index" in x) for x in obj):
            n = max(int(x["index"]) for x in obj) + 1
            classes = [None]*n
            for x in obj:
                classes[int(x["index"])] = x.get("name", str(x.get("label", "?")))
            return classes
        return [x.get("name", str(x.get("label", f"class_{i}"))) if isinstance(x, dict) else str(x)
                for i, x in enumerate(obj)]
    return []

def load_classes(label_map_path, ckpt):
    # Prefer classes embedded in checkpoint, fall back to label_map.json
    if isinstance(ckpt, dict) and "classes" in ckpt and isinstance(ckpt["classes"], (list, dict)):
        cls_from_ckpt = normalize_label_map(ckpt["classes"])
        cls_from_ckpt = [c for c in cls_from_ckpt if c is not None]
        if len(cls_from_ckpt) > 0:
            print(f"Loaded {len(cls_from_ckpt)} classes from checkpoint.")
            return cls_from_ckpt

    with open(label_map_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        raw = json.load(f)
    classes = normalize_label_map(raw)
    classes = [c for c in classes if c is not None]
    print(f"Loaded {len(classes)} classes from label_map.json")
    return classes

def extract_state_dict(ckpt):
    # Handles multiple formats
    if isinstance(ckpt, dict):
        if "model_state" in ckpt and isinstance(ckpt["model_state"], dict):
            return ckpt["model_state"]
        if "state_dict" in ckpt and isinstance(ckpt["state_dict"], dict):
            return ckpt["state_dict"]
        # maybe already a state_dict (keys like 'net.0.weight')
        if any(isinstance(k, str) and (k.startswith("net.") or k.startswith("classifier.")) for k in ckpt.keys()):
            return ckpt
    # fallback: assume ckpt is a valid state_dict
    return ckpt

def build_items(proc_dir, classes):
    items = []
    for i, cls in enumerate(classes):
        for fp in glob(os.path.join(proc_dir, cls, "*.npy")):
            items.append((fp, i))
    return items

def split_items(items, train_split=0.78, seed=1337):
    random.Random(seed).shuffle(items)
    n_train = int(len(items) * train_split)
    return items[:n_train], items[n_train:]

def plot_confusion(cm, class_names, out_png):
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10,10))
    im = ax.imshow(cm, interpolation='nearest')
    ax.figure.colorbar(im, ax=ax)
    ax.set(xticks=np.arange(cm.shape[1]),
           yticks=np.arange(cm.shape[0]),
           xticklabels=class_names, yticklabels=class_names,

           title='Confusion Matrix (Validation)')
    plt.setp(ax.get_xticklabels(), rotation=90, ha="center")
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig(out_png, dpi=200)
    plt.close(fig)

def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Evaluate frog model on validation split.")
    ap.add_argument("--processed", default=PROC_DIR)
    ap.add_argument("--model", default=DEFAULT_MODEL)
    ap.add_argument("--label-map", default=DEFAULT_LABELMAP)
    ap.add_argument("--train-split", type=float, default=0.78)
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=1337)
    ap.add_argument("--frames", type=int, default=None, help="Override frames; default pulls from checkpoint if present, else 100")
    ap.add_argument("--batch", type=int, default=64)
    args = ap.parse_args()

    # Load checkpoint first (for classes/frames & state)
    ckpt = torch.load(args.model, map_location="cpu")
    classes = load_classes(args.label_map, ckpt)

    # Determine target frames
    target_frames = args.frames
    if target_frames is None and isinstance(ckpt, dict) and "frames" in ckpt:
        target_frames = int(ckpt["frames"])
    if target_frames is None:
        target_frames = 100
    print(f"Using target frames: {target_frames}")

    # Build items only for those classes
    all_items = build_items(args.processed, classes)
    train_items, val_items = split_items(all_items, train_split=args.train_split, seed=args.seed)
    print(f"Classes: {len(classes)} | Train: {len(train_items)} | Val: {len(val_items)}")
    if len(val_items) == 0:
        print("No validation items found. Check your label_map/classes and processed data.")
        return

    val_ds = MFCCDataset(val_items, target_frames=target_frames, add_channel_dim=True)
    val_loader = DataLoader(val_ds, batch_size=args.batch, shuffle=False, num_workers=0, pin_memory=False)

    # Build model & load state dict
    device = torch.device("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")
    model = SmallCNN(n_classes=len(classes))
    state_dict = extract_state_dict(ckpt)
    missing, unexpected = model.load_state_dict(state_dict, strict=False)
    if missing or unexpected:
        print(f"⚠️ load_state_dict warnings — missing: {missing}, unexpected: {unexpected}")
    model.to(device).eval()

    # Evaluate
    y_true, y_pred = [], []
    with torch.no_grad():
        for xb, yb in val_loader:
            xb = xb.to(device, non_blocking=True)
            logits = model(xb)
            pred = torch.argmax(logits, dim=1).cpu().numpy().tolist()

            y_true.extend(yb.numpy().tolist())

    # Metrics
    acc = accuracy_score(y_true, y_pred)
    f1_micro = f1_score(y_true, y_pred, average="micro")
    f1_macro = f1_score(y_true, y_pred, average="macro")
    prec, rec, f1, support = precision_recall_fscore_support(
        y_true, y_pred, labels=list(range(len(classes))), zero_division=0
    )

    print(f"\nOverall:")
    print(f"  Accuracy: {acc:.3f}")
    print(f"  F1 (micro): {f1_micro:.3f}")
    print(f"  F1 (macro): {f1_macro:.3f}")

    print("\nPer-class: name | n | precision | recall | f1")
    order = np.argsort(-support)
    for idx in order[:20]:
        print(f"  {classes[idx]:<28} | {int(support[idx]):4d} | {prec[idx]:6.2f} | {rec[idx]:6.2f} | {f1[idx]:6.2f}")

    # Confusion matrix & outputs
    cm = confusion_matrix(y_true, y_pred, labels=list(range(len(classes))))
    os.makedirs(MODEL_DIR, exist_ok=True)
    cm_png = os.path.join(MODEL_DIR, "confusion_matrix_val.png")
    plot_confusion(cm, classes, cm_png)
    print(f"\n📈 Confusion matrix saved to: {cm_png}")

        f.write(classification_report(y_true, y_pred, target_names=classes, zero_division=0))
    print(f"📄 Detailed report: {report_txt}")

Nice! We can see exactly what’s wrong:

Your checkpoint uses layer names features.* (not net.*) and its classifier has Dropout at index 1 and Linear layers at indices 2 and 5.

My previous eval class expected Linear at 1 and 4, so almost none of the weights loaded → random model → 0% acc.

classification_report blew up because it inferred only the seen classes from y_true. We need to pass labels=range(len(classes)).

Here’s a drop-in fixed eval script that mirrors your training model naming/shapes (so weights load cleanly) and also fixes the report:

# FrogSoundProject/src/eval_from_loader.py
import os, json, argparse, random, numpy as np
from glob import glob

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
from torch.utils.data import Dataset, DataLoader

from sklearn.metrics import accuracy_score, f1_score, precision_recall_fscore_support, confusion_matrix, classification_report
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

PROC_DIR = os.path.join("FrogSoundProject", "data", "processed")
MODEL_DIR = os.path.join("FrogSoundProject", "models")
DEFAULT_MODEL = os.path.join(MODEL_DIR, "frog_cnn_best.pt")
DEFAULT_LABELMAP = os.path.join(MODEL_DIR, "label_map.json")

# ---------- Dataset ----------
class MFCCDataset(Dataset):
    def __init__(self, items, target_frames=100, add_channel_dim=True):
        self.items = items
        self.T = target_frames
        self.add_channel = add_channel_dim

    def __len__(self):
        return len(self.items)

    def _pad_or_crop(self, a):
        c, t = a.shape
        if t < self.T:
            pad = np.zeros((c, self.T - t), dtype=a.dtype)
            a = np.concatenate([a, pad], axis=1)
        elif t > self.T:
            a = a[:, :self.T]
        return a

    def __getitem__(self, idx):
        path, y = self.items[idx]
        a = np.load(path)
        if a.ndim == 3:
            a = a.squeeze(-1)
        a = a.astype(np.float32)
        a = self._pad_or_crop(a)
        if self.add_channel:
            a = a[None, ...]  # (1, 13, T)
        return torch.from_numpy(a), y

# ---------- Model (match training names/indices) ----------
class SmallCNN(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, n_classes, in_ch=1):
        super().__init__()
        # names must be "features.*" to match checkpoint
        self.features = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(in_ch, 16, 3, padding=1),     # 0
            nn.BatchNorm2d(16),                     # 1
            nn.ReLU(),                              # 2
            nn.MaxPool2d((1, 2)),                   # 3
            nn.Conv2d(16, 32, 3, padding=1),        # 4
            nn.BatchNorm2d(32),                     # 5
            nn.ReLU(),                              # 6
            nn.MaxPool2d((1, 2)),                   # 7
            nn.Conv2d(32, 64, 3, padding=1),        # 8
            nn.BatchNorm2d(64),                     # 9
            nn.ReLU(),                              #10
            nn.AdaptiveMaxPool2d((13, 25)),         #11
        )
        # classifier indices with weights at 2 and 5, per your checkpoint
        self.classifier = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Flatten(),                           # 0
            nn.Dropout(0.0),                        # 1 (no weights)
            nn.Linear(64*13*25, 256),               # 2 (weights present)
            nn.ReLU(),                              # 3
            nn.Dropout(0.3),                        # 4 (no weights)
            nn.Linear(256, n_classes),              # 5 (weights present)
        )

    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.features(x)
        return self.classifier(x)

# ---------- Helpers ----------
def normalize_label_map(obj):
    if isinstance(obj, dict):
        if all(isinstance(v, int) for v in obj.values()):
            n = max(obj.values()) + 1
            classes = [None]*n
            for name, idx in obj.items():
                classes[idx] = name
            return classes
        if all(str(k).isdigit() for k in obj.keys()):
            items = {int(k): v for k, v in obj.items()}
            n = max(items.keys()) + 1
            classes = [None]*n
            for idx, name in items.items():
                classes[idx] = name
            return classes
        return list(obj.keys())

    if isinstance(obj, list):
        if not obj:
            return []
        if all(isinstance(x, str) for x in obj):
            return list(obj)
        if all(isinstance(x, dict) and ("index" in x) for x in obj):
            n = max(int(x["index"]) for x in obj) + 1
            classes = [None]*n
            for x in obj:
                classes[int(x["index"])] = x.get("name", str(x.get("label", "?")))
            return classes
        return [x.get("name", str(x.get("label", f"class_{i}"))) if isinstance(x, dict) else str(x)
                for i, x in enumerate(obj)]
    return []

def load_classes(label_map_path, ckpt):
    if isinstance(ckpt, dict) and "classes" in ckpt and isinstance(ckpt["classes"], (list, dict)):
        cls_from_ckpt = normalize_label_map(ckpt["classes"])
        cls_from_ckpt = [c for c in cls_from_ckpt if c is not None]
        if len(cls_from_ckpt) > 0:
            print(f"Loaded {len(cls_from_ckpt)} classes from checkpoint.")
            return cls_from_ckpt
    with open(label_map_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        raw = json.load(f)
    classes = normalize_label_map(raw)
    classes = [c for c in classes if c is not None]
    print(f"Loaded {len(classes)} classes from label_map.json")
    return classes

def extract_state_dict(ckpt):
    if isinstance(ckpt, dict):
        if "model_state" in ckpt and isinstance(ckpt["model_state"], dict):
            return ckpt["model_state"]
        if "state_dict" in ckpt and isinstance(ckpt["state_dict"], dict):
            return ckpt["state_dict"]
        if any(isinstance(k, str) and (k.startswith("features.") or k.startswith("classifier.")) for k in ckpt.keys()):
            return ckpt
    return ckpt

def build_items(proc_dir, classes):
    items = []
    for i, cls in enumerate(classes):
        for fp in glob(os.path.join(proc_dir, cls, "*.npy")):
            items.append((fp, i))
    return items

def split_items(items, train_split=0.78, seed=1337):
    random.Random(seed).shuffle(items)
    n_train = int(len(items) * train_split)
    return items[:n_train], items[n_train:]

def plot_confusion(cm, class_names, out_png):
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10,10))
    im = ax.imshow(cm, interpolation='nearest')
    ax.figure.colorbar(im, ax=ax)
    ax.set(xticks=np.arange(cm.shape[1]),
           yticks=np.arange(cm.shape[0]),
           xticklabels=class_names, yticklabels=class_names,
           ylabel='True label', xlabel='Predicted label',
           title='Confusion Matrix (Validation)')
    plt.setp(ax.get_xticklabels(), rotation=90, ha="center")
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig(out_png, dpi=200)
    plt.close(fig)

def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Evaluate frog model on validation split.")
    ap.add_argument("--processed", default=PROC_DIR)
    ap.add_argument("--model", default=DEFAULT_MODEL)
    ap.add_argument("--label-map", default=DEFAULT_LABELMAP)
    ap.add_argument("--train-split", type=float, default=0.78)
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=1337)
    ap.add_argument("--frames", type=int, default=None, help="Override frames; default uses checkpoint if present, else 100")
    ap.add_argument("--batch", type=int, default=64)
    args = ap.parse_args()

    # Load checkpoint & classes
    ckpt = torch.load(args.model, map_location="cpu")
    classes = load_classes(args.label_map, ckpt)

    # Frames
    target_frames = args.frames if args.frames is not None else int(ckpt.get("frames", 100))
    print(f"Using target frames: {target_frames}")

    # Build splits
    all_items = build_items(args.processed, classes)
    train_items, val_items = split_items(all_items, train_split=args.train_split, seed=args.seed)
    print(f"Classes: {len(classes)} | Train: {len(train_items)} | Val: {len(val_items)}")
    if len(val_items) == 0:
        print("No validation items found. Aborting.")
        return

    val_loader = DataLoader(
        MFCCDataset(val_items, target_frames=target_frames, add_channel_dim=True),
        batch_size=args.batch, shuffle=False, num_workers=0, pin_memory=False
    )

    # Build model & load weights
    device = torch.device("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")
    model = SmallCNN(n_classes=len(classes))
    state_dict = extract_state_dict(ckpt)
    missing, unexpected = model.load_state_dict(state_dict, strict=False)
    if missing or unexpected:
        print(f"⚠️ load_state_dict warnings — missing: {missing}, unexpected: {unexpected}")
    model.to(device).eval()

    # Eval
    y_true, y_pred = [], []
    with torch.no_grad():
        for xb, yb in val_loader:
            xb = xb.to(device, non_blocking=True)
            logits = model(xb)
            pred = torch.argmax(logits, dim=1).cpu().numpy().tolist()
            y_pred.extend(pred)
            y_true.extend(yb.numpy().tolist())

    # Metrics
    labels = list(range(len(classes)))
    acc = accuracy_score(y_true, y_pred)
    f1_micro = f1_score(y_true, y_pred, average="micro", labels=labels)
    f1_macro = f1_score(y_true, y_pred, average="macro", labels=labels)
    prec, rec, f1, support = precision_recall_fscore_support(
        y_true, y_pred, labels=labels, zero_division=0
    )

    print(f"\nOverall:")
    print(f"  Accuracy: {acc:.3f}")
    print(f"  F1 (micro): {f1_micro:.3f}")
    print(f"  F1 (macro): {f1_macro:.3f}")

    print("\nPer-class: name | n | precision | recall | f1")
    order = np.argsort(-support)
    for idx in order[:20]:
        print(f"  {classes[idx]:<28} | {int(support[idx]):4d} | {prec[idx]:6.2f} | {rec[idx]:6.2f} | {f1[idx]:6.2f}")

    # Confusion matrix & outputs
    cm = confusion_matrix(y_true, y_pred, labels=labels)
    os.makedirs(MODEL_DIR, exist_ok=True)
    cm_png = os.path.join(MODEL_DIR, "confusion_matrix_val.png")
    plot_confusion(cm, classes, cm_png)
    print(f"\n📈 Confusion matrix saved to: {cm_png}")

    out_csv = os.path.join(MODEL_DIR, "val_predictions.csv")
    with open(out_csv, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write("true_label,true_name,pred_label,pred_name\n")
        for t, p in zip(y_true, y_pred):
            f.write(f"{t},{classes[t]},{p},{classes[p]}\n")
    print(f"📝 Predictions CSV: {out_csv}")

    report_txt = os.path.join(MODEL_DIR, "classification_report.txt")
    with open(report_txt, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(classification_report(y_true, y_pred, labels=labels, target_names=classes, zero_division=0))
    print(f"📄 Detailed report: {report_txt}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Ah—your checkpoint’s FC layer expects an input size of 832, but our eval model was flattening to 64×13×25 = 20 800. That means the model you trained ended with a pooling to (13, 1) (so 64×13×1 = 832). Let’s make the eval model adapt to whatever the checkpoint expects.

# FrogSoundProject/src/eval_from_loader.py
import os, json, argparse, random, numpy as np
from glob import glob

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
from torch.utils.data import Dataset, DataLoader

from sklearn.metrics import (
    accuracy_score, f1_score,
    precision_recall_fscore_support,
    confusion_matrix, classification_report
)
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

PROC_DIR = os.path.join("FrogSoundProject", "data", "processed")
MODEL_DIR = os.path.join("FrogSoundProject", "models")
DEFAULT_MODEL = os.path.join(MODEL_DIR, "frog_cnn_best.pt")
DEFAULT_LABELMAP = os.path.join(MODEL_DIR, "label_map.json")

# ---------- Dataset ----------
class MFCCDataset(Dataset):
    def __init__(self, items, target_frames=100, add_channel_dim=True):
        self.items = items
        self.T = target_frames
        self.add_channel = add_channel_dim

    def __len__(self):
        return len(self.items)

    def _pad_or_crop(self, a):
        c, t = a.shape
        if t < self.T:
            pad = np.zeros((c, self.T - t), dtype=a.dtype)
            a = np.concatenate([a, pad], axis=1)
        elif t > self.T:
            a = a[:, :self.T]
        return a

    def __getitem__(self, idx):
        path, y = self.items[idx]
        a = np.load(path)
        if a.ndim == 3:
            a = a.squeeze(-1)
        a = a.astype(np.float32)
        a = self._pad_or_crop(a)
        if self.add_channel:
            a = a[None, ...]  # (1, 13, T)
        return torch.from_numpy(a), y

# ---------- Model (features/classifier names must match checkpoint) ----------
class SmallCNN(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, n_classes, pool_time_bins=1, in_ch=1, classifier_in=None):
        super().__init__()
        self.features = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(in_ch, 16, 3, padding=1),     # 0
            nn.BatchNorm2d(16),                     # 1
            nn.ReLU(),                              # 2
            nn.MaxPool2d((1, 2)),                   # 3
            nn.Conv2d(16, 32, 3, padding=1),        # 4
            nn.BatchNorm2d(32),                     # 5
            nn.ReLU(),                              # 6
            nn.MaxPool2d((1, 2)),                   # 7
            nn.Conv2d(32, 64, 3, padding=1),        # 8
            nn.BatchNorm2d(64),                     # 9
            nn.ReLU(),                              # 10
            # We’ll set the time bins dynamically; freq is fixed at 13
            nn.AdaptiveMaxPool2d((13, pool_time_bins)),  # 11
        )
        in_feats = classifier_in if classifier_in is not None else 64 * 13 * pool_time_bins
        self.classifier = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Flatten(),                           # 0
            nn.Dropout(0.0),                        # 1  (no weights; matches your checkpoint indexing)
            nn.Linear(in_feats, 256),               # 2  (has weights)
            nn.ReLU(),                              # 3
            nn.Dropout(0.3),                        # 4  (no weights)
            nn.Linear(256, n_classes),              # 5  (has weights)
        )

    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.features(x)
        return self.classifier(x)

# ---------- Helpers ----------

        if all(isinstance(x, str) for x in obj):

                for i, x in enumerate(obj)]
    return []

    args = ap.parse_args()

    # Load checkpoint & classes
    ckpt = torch.load(args.model, map_location="cpu")
    classes = load_classes(args.label_map, ckpt)

    # Frames
    target_frames = args.frames if args.frames is not None else int(ckpt.get("frames", 100))
    print(f"Using target frames: {target_frames}")

    # Build splits
    all_items = build_items(args.processed, classes)
    train_items, val_items = split_items(all_items, train_split=args.train_split, seed=args.seed)
    print(f"Classes: {len(classes)} | Train: {len(train_items)} | Val: {len(val_items)}")
    if len(val_items) == 0:
        print("No validation items found. Aborting.")
        return

    val_loader = DataLoader(
        MFCCDataset(val_items, target_frames=target_frames, add_channel_dim=True),
        batch_size=args.batch, shuffle=False, num_workers=0, pin_memory=False
    )

    # Figure out the FC input size expected by the checkpoint
    state_dict = extract_state_dict(ckpt)
    if "classifier.2.weight" not in state_dict:
        raise RuntimeError("Checkpoint does not contain 'classifier.2.weight'; cannot infer FC size.")
    fc_in_from_ckpt = state_dict["classifier.2.weight"].shape[1]   # e.g., 832
    # infer pool_time_bins given conv out channels (64) and freq bins 13
    if fc_in_from_ckpt % (64*13) != 0:
        raise RuntimeError(f"Unexpected FC in_features {fc_in_from_ckpt}; not divisible by 64*13.")
    pool_time_bins = fc_in_from_ckpt // (64*13)

    # Build model to MATCH checkpoint geometry exactly
    model = SmallCNN(n_classes=len(classes), pool_time_bins=pool_time_bins, classifier_in=fc_in_from_ckpt)
    missing, unexpected = model.load_state_dict(state_dict, strict=False)
    if missing or unexpected:
        print(f"⚠️ load_state_dict warnings — missing: {missing}, unexpected: {unexpected}")

    device = torch.device("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")
    model.to(device).eval()

    # Eval
    y_true, y_pred = [], []
    with torch.no_grad():
        for xb, yb in val_loader:
            xb = xb.to(device, non_blocking=True)
            logits = model(xb)
            pred = torch.argmax(logits, dim=1).cpu().numpy().tolist()
            y_pred.extend(pred)
            y_true.extend(yb.numpy().tolist())

    # Metrics
    labels = list(range(len(classes)))
    acc = accuracy_score(y_true, y_pred)
    f1_micro = f1_score(y_true, y_pred, average="micro", labels=labels)
    f1_macro = f1_score(y_true, y_pred, average="macro", labels=labels)
    prec, rec, f1, support = precision_recall_fscore_support(
        y_true, y_pred, labels=labels, zero_division=0
    )

    print(f"\nOverall:")
    print(f"  Accuracy: {acc:.3f}")
    print(f"  F1 (micro): {f1_micro:.3f}")
    print(f"  F1 (macro): {f1_macro:.3f}")

    print("\nPer-class: name | n | precision | recall | f1")
    order = np.argsort(-support)
    for idx in order[:20]:
        print(f"  {classes[idx]:<28} | {int(support[idx]):4d} | {prec[idx]:6.2f} | {rec[idx]:6.2f} | {f1[idx]:6.2f}")

    # Confusion matrix & outputs
    cm = confusion_matrix(y_true, y_pred, labels=labels)
    os.makedirs(MODEL_DIR, exist_ok=True)
    cm_png = os.path.join(MODEL_DIR, "confusion_matrix_val.png")
    plot_confusion(cm, classes, cm_png)
    print(f"\n📈 Confusion matrix saved to: {cm_png}")

    out_csv = os.path.join(MODEL_DIR, "val_predictions.csv")
    with open(out_csv, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write("true_label,true_name,pred_label,pred_name\n")
        for t, p in zip(y_true, y_pred):
            f.write(f"{t},{classes[t]},{p},{classes[p]}\n")
    print(f"📝 Predictions CSV: {out_csv}")

    report_txt = os.path.join(MODEL_DIR, "classification_report.txt")
    with open(report_txt, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(classification_report(y_true, y_pred, labels=labels, target_names=classes, zero_division=0))
    print(f"📄 Detailed report: {report_txt}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
Then run:

Why this fixes it:

We read the expected in_features from classifier.2.weight in your checkpoint (832) and adapt pooling to produce exactly that (which implies pooling to (13, 1)).

We keep your layer names/indices (features.*, classifier.2, classifier.5) so weights slot in perfectly.

We pass labels=range(n_classes) to all sklearn metrics, so the report/CSV/CM are consistent even if a few classes don’t appear in the current val split.
